result.title: AI Teaches Humans to Handle Complexity in the Game of Go
result.summary: Strategic decision-making in complex environments requires balancing local stability against global coordination. Using the game of Go as a bounded empirical testbed, we investigate how biological and artificial agents navigate this trade-off by formalizing a network-derived metric of strategic tension defined via the spectral radius of spatial dependency matrices. Across human skill progression, tension systematically decays from novices to masters as uncoordinated tactical skirmishes give way to disciplined territorial stabilization. However, a longitudinal analysis of professional play spanning 1980--2026 reveals a striking historical paradox: following the superhuman breakthrough of AlphaGo in 2016, elite human matches display a marked surge in sustained tension. A two-dimensional projection based on move distance and captures places modern professionals close to neural engines, separating their tension from the local contact fighting of novices and from random noise. Consequently, strategic tension acts as a macroscopic order parameter for decision paradigms rather than raw computational strength. Beyond the game of Go, these findings establish a constructive paradigm for human-AI interaction, indicating how artificial systems can act as cognitive scaffolding that expands biological heuristics and elevates human capacity to navigate higher-order complexity across professional training and decision-making domains.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以围棋为经验测试平台，提出由空间依赖矩阵谱半径刻画的「战略张力」指标，比较新手到大师的水平演进及1980–2026年职业棋谱，发现2016年AlphaGo之后顶尖人类对局的持续张力显著上升，并主张张力是决策范式的宏观序参量而非算力强弱。
AI.relevance_reason: 用网络谱特征把「局部接触」与「全局协调」的权衡压缩为单一序参量，或可供核查作为诊断 LVR 中视觉证据局部使用与全局推理状态协调程度的量化线索；但该文分析人类棋谱行为与棋力，不涉及 VLM 内部 latent 状态，联系仅在概念与度量层面。
